text:
Maeve (Finance): QuotaForge renewal proposal landed in my inbox — there's an "overage smoothing credit" line that doesn't match the math. Can someone eyeball? :thinking:

Maeve (Finance): Here are the invoice lines they sent (redacted):
```
PO: PF-3321
Commit: $30,000/mo (100M tokens)
Usage: 118,600,000 tokens
Overage charge: $2,364
Overage smoothing credit: $1,200
Final due: $31,164
```

Jules (Procurement): pinging @Owen and @Nina. Do we know which SKU QuotaForge maps tokens to? The $/token and rounding could explain it.

Owen (Platform): They bill two SKUs: transformer.tokens ($0.00002/token) and access.stream ($50/month per stream). If we assume all usage billed as transformer.tokens -> 18.6M * $0.00002 = $372. That's not matching. Might be bundled per-request surcharges or quantization add-ons.

Nina (Billing): I pulled the billing export for May — they sent a summary, but line-level CSV has a code CF-SMOOTH applied after preliminary calc. Full CSV snippet: 
```
line_id,sku,units,unit_price,subtotal,credit_code,credit_amt
L001,transformer.tokens,118600000,0.00002,2372, ,0
L002,commit_discount,100000000, -0.00001,-1000, ,0
L003,overage_smoothing,18600000,0.000064,1190,CF-SMOOTH,1200
```
So they applied a smoothing credit of 1200 but the math for L003 subtotal looks off by 10.

Maeve (Finance): Exactly — vendor's line-level math doesn't reconcile to final due. Also contract says smoothing should never increase billed amount vs raw calc.

Iris (BillingBot): Invoice PF-3321 flagged: anomaly_score=0.87. Suggested action=manual-review + vendor clarification.

Jules (Procurement): Action items: 1) Ask QuotaForge for detailed compute of CF-SMOOTH formula and why L003 subtotal != credit_amt. 2) Ask for commit true-up language to be explicit in renewal. I'll draft the email.

Sam (Legal): Add: request explicit sample calculation in the contract (appendix) and a clause that credits are applied on a per-invoice basis with parity to raw usage calc. If they refuse, propose a 6mo pilot extension instead of 12mo commit.

Owen (Platform): Quick ask for engineering context: can we flatten traffic for next month to see how smoothing behaves? If smoothing depends on burst patterns we can simulate. Happy to run a 7-day sample if procurement requests it.

Maeve (Finance): Good. Jules, can you include the PO and ask for matching CSV with line totals and formula? Also request that any credit codes be exported as separate fields so Billing's parser doesn't lose them.

Jules (Procurement): On it. Drafting now, will post the mail thread for review before sending. Expect send by EOD. :thumbsup:

Nina (Billing): FYI, if they can't give transparent formula, our fallback is to refuse the smoothing credit and ask for raw true-up math in the invoice. That makes automation easier.

Maeve (Finance): Thanks. If QuotaForge pushes hard on price, we should consider negotiating a capped overage rate or a blended CPI for 12 months. I'll prepare the suggested numbers after Jules posts the draft. :eyes:
